Subject: Architecture clarifications + scaling playbook request (Finova)

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for taking the product deep-dive today. Quick recap of what we heard and a short list of asks so our scoping team can size Dedicated for your core inference path: 

Key constraints we captured
- Peak inference workload: ~1,200 peak qps for short prompts (avg len ~80 tokens) and 400 qps for embeddings/reranker flows.
- Latency goal: P95 < 150ms for standard text gen calls; embeddings P99 goal ~= 250ms.
- Multi-tenant routing: single VPC; want per-tenant isolation via routing tags; sensitive workloads must be routed to isolated pools.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline at ~200 qps with spikes up to peak for 2-3 hrs/day.

Asks for sizing + design (please provide by EOD Mon if possible):
1) Network egress / NAT throughput and any proxy limits we should know about.
2) Expected concurrency per user/session that issues long-running tool-calls (you mentioned tool invoking external rerankers).
3) Any planned throttling windows or blackout windows for deploys.
4) Confirmation of retention policy for logs / KV caches (30 days default?)

I attached a short template (finova_infra_req.xlsx) that captures the fields our infra team needs to propose a Dedicated cluster. Also included a placeholder link to our sizing template — if you can fill the highlighted rows it will speed the internal quote.

Next step proposal: our infra folks want to model two autoscale tiers — baseline (autoscale to 2x baseline w/ short-burst queues) and emergency fallback (lower-cost model variant with higher quantization). If that sounds reasonable I can sketch numbers and share a canary timeline.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek —

Appreciate the detailed recap. Quick answers inline below and a couple of clarifications: 

1) Network / proxy: we have outbound egress through a pair of NAT gateways (10 Gbps total). No additional proxy that throttles TCP sessions, but we do have an internal WAF that may inspect HTTPS.
2) Concurrency: our UI issues up to 6 simultaneous `generate` calls per end-user session during heavy annotation workflows; the reranker pipeline is batched every 3s with up to 256 items per batch.
3) Blackouts: we have a nightly maintenance window 02:00–02:30 UTC where deploys are restricted. No other blackout windows currently planned.
4) Retention: logs retained 90 days; application-level cache retention is 7 days by default but we can extend.

I attached a simple network diagram (network_diagram_v1.pdf) showing the VPC layout and NAT placement. We'll try to fill your spreadsheet by Monday morning.

Two questions for your sizing model:
- How do you recommend dimensioning queues for the short burst traffic vs steady state?
- For the reranker/embeddings path, is there a preferred batching approach in Redwood Dedicated (time-based vs size-based) to balance throughput and P95 latency?

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of AI Platform — Finova

Alice —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the network details. A few technical notes from our sizing/serving team and a short set of asks to help us produce a concrete Dedicated capacity recommendation: 

Notes / recommendations
- Queueing model: we typically recommend a hybrid queue design — time-windowed batching for embeddings/rerankers (e.g., 3–5ms window with early release at 256 items) and size-based batching for low-latency text generation (batch cap 8–16, adaptive). That gives stable throughput for embeddings while keeping P95 low for generation.
- Autoscale tiers: baseline (1x baseline pool sized for sustained 200 qps), scale-up pool (adds capacity up to 4x baseline on spike alert), and fallbacks (quantized variant with ~25% lower memory/use per GPU).
- Concurrency limits: recommend per-request concurrency of 16 for gen calls per GPU worker, and an overall per-customer concurrency cap to avoid noisy neighbors — we typically propose an initial cap of 400 concurrent requests per customer with a soft-throttle policy.
- Queues: short-burst queue with token-based prioritization and a decode-time budget to prevent queue starvation during large spikes.

Asks (if you can confirm these it will speed the sizing):
A) Typical per-call token counts for the gen paths (mean and 95th).
B) Whether the reranker batch window can be widened to 5s in the event of heavy spikes (this helps throughput but increases tail latency).
C) Any regulatory requirement that would prevent the use of quantized fallback models for certain datasets.

I've attached our Dedicated sizing template (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.csv) with the recommended defaults filled in — please update the highlighted cells with your actual numbers and we will convert to a cost + capacity proposal.

Proposed next step: brief technical workshop (30–45m) with your infra and our serving runtime team to lock the queue thresholds and canary rollout plan. Are you available Wed 20 Jan 14:00 PT?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Typical token counts: gen mean ~95 tokens, gen 95th ~420 tokens. Embeddings payloads avg 64 tokens.
- Reranker window: we can widen to 4s during spikes, but 5s would be marginal; can we architect a dynamic window?
- Quantized fallback: permitted for internal data, not for PII-bearing datasets. We'll flag datasets that require full-precision.

Wed 20 Jan 14:00 PT works for Alice and me — please send a calendar invite. One ask for that call: can you bring a short runbook that maps autoscale triggers to concrete GPU count changes (we want to see simulated ramp numbers)?

— Bob

Thanks Bob — great context.

I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 20 Jan 14:00 PT and we'll include: Marissa, Marcus (serving runtime), and one of our infra engineers to walk the runtime-to-GPU mapping.

Preview of the runbook items we'll cover on the call (so you can prep):
- Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU util thresholds + queue depth + short-burst queue fill percentage.
- Concrete mapping: how a 2x queue depth spike maps to additional GPU slices in our Dedicated model (we'll show numbers for your 200 → 1,200 qps scenario).
- Canary plan: 10% traffic canary for 24 hours with automatic rollback on P95 regressions (we will propose a P95 SLA guardrail at 200ms for gen calls during canary).
- Routing: per-tenant tag rules and an emergency circuit that routes sensitive traffic to isolated pools.

Action items before the call:
- Finova: fill the highlighted cells in the sizing CSV and flag datasets that must avoid quantized fallbacks (Bob/Alice).
- Redwood: we will produce a first-pass autoscale + GPU mapping PDF and a short runbook by Tue EOD.

I'll share the invite and the prep artifacts shortly. Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
